clue.text: Mean to pay a visit but have a narrow escape

parts.note: mean in the stingy sense is close, as in close-fisted
to call on someone is to pay them a visit

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to visit a friend and has a lucky brush with danger on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like 'intend', but here it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss with disaster, escaped only just, is described by this idiom.

clue.text: The international river of the underworld

parts.note: 'the' given in two languages: le is the French word, then the English one
'the' given in two languages: le is the French word, then the English one

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding description of a mythical river that crosses borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The international' asks for the word 'the' in more than one language: French LE followed by English THE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the dead drank from this river of forgetfulness in Hades.

clue.text: Where one might find various classes of fish

definitions.text: Where one might find various classes of fish

parts.words: Where one might find various classes of fish
parts.note: reads as a place of lessons in different year groups, but a group of fish swimming together is also given this name

explanation.surface: A biology lesson on the different classes of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Educational establishment holding many classes, and also the collective noun for a shoal of fish.

clue.text: One animal let out, or a herd of them?

parts.note: a cat is one kind of animal

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of let are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether one beast was released, or a whole herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET to make TLE, which follows CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and bullocks kept together in a herd are livestock of this kind.

clue.text: It is not far to the inn

explanation.surface: Directions given to a thirsty traveller asking for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearby is described as neighbourhood-based, and the neighbourhood pub is called one's own in British speech.

clue.text: Rusty, having been struck off

explanation.surface: A doctor whose skills have lapsed after being barred from medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty means lacking recent experience; a struck-off doctor is no longer allowed to run a surgery.

clue.text: Like a lettuce perhaps, full of compassion

explanation.surface: Comparing a kind person to a soft-centred salad vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettuce has a soft core, and a kindly sympathetic person is said to have a soft heart.

clue.text: Exactly what is needed to gain admission

explanation.surface: Someone says a pass is all you need to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely the right thing; literally, a pass is required for entry.

clue.text: Friar says he is unable to put it right

parts.note: to put something right is to mend it
someone saying he is unable says I can't

explanation.surface: A friar admits he cannot fix the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The friar's words 'I can't mend' are rearranged so MEND comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Begging orders of friars, such as Franciscans, are called this kind of order.

clue.text: Score three less

parts.note: a score is twenty, and taking three from that leaves a number in the teens

explanation.surface: A sports result where a team scored three fewer points.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty minus three gives this number.

clue.text: The Spanish work with energy to make a bolt

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
op is short for opus, a musical work
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Spanish workers put energy into making a bolt in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like a piece of hardware, but it means running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to marry are said to do this, a sudden flight.

clue.text: Deposit for a house

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit to buy a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to lodge it, as with a complaint; and a gatekeeper's cottage is so called.

clue.text: Neil perplexed follows a stranger

indicators.note: follows puts the rearranged name after the article
perplexed suggests the letters of the name Neil are muddled up

explanation.surface: Puzzled Neil tails a stranger down the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perplexed' turns NEIL into LIEN, which 'follows' the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider or foreigner is someone from elsewhere.

clue.text: A tax on a coral island

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax, as for using a road

explanation.surface: A tourist levy imposed on a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped reef of coral enclosing a lagoon has this name.

clue.text: One French boy or girl

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
René is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: A French child of uncertain sex.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name.

clue.text: Approaches northern listeners

parts.note: ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: Someone sidles up to an audience in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To come closer to something is to approach it.

clue.text: Portray some rude pictures

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist is asked to paint some saucy images.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to show it in a picture or words.

clue.text: Freedom of access of course

explanation.surface: A diner's right to enter, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but defines a dish served at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means right of entry, and also a dish served as a main or starter course.

clue.text: Theatre for musical works

explanation.surface: A venue where music is performed.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera house is a theatre, and the plural of opus names several musical compositions.

clue.text: Man found by the Spanish church

parts.note: chap is informal for a man
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A man spotted near a Spanish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A small place of worship, often in a school or hospital.

clue.text: Fresh from the centre

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of the letters of centre, rearranged

explanation.surface: Produce brought fresh from the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that CENTRE's letters are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new or of late is fresh.

clue.text: Grounds holding a large number in northern England

indicators.note: holding says one word encloses another

parts.note: coffee grounds or wine dregs are lees
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Football grounds packed with fans somewhere in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEDS is a city in Yorkshire in northern England; 'Grounds' suggests football stadiums but means sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Yorkshire city lies in that part of the country.

clue.text: Inspire affection despite having neared disaster

indicators.note: disaster suggests the letters of neared are wrecked and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone wins hearts after a near catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: To make oneself loved or liked by others.

clue.text: Famine for hundreds on this planet

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral five hundred, several hundreds
our planet is Earth

explanation.surface: Hunger affecting hundreds across the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity or lack, especially of food.

clue.text: It isn't the newsman who is famous

parts.note: isn't gives not
ed is short for editor, the man in charge of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Denying that a celebrity is the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Well known or celebrated people are distinguished.

clue.text: The same again, mostly affluent architecture

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: affluent means rich

explanation.surface: Wealthy owners repeat the same grand building style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The same again' reads like a bar order but is ditto, DO.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical orders of Greek columns.

clue.text: Swear when I leave the cruise, shipwrecked

indicators.note: shipwrecked suggests the remaining letters of cruise are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone swears as the cruise ship is wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I leave' removes the I from CRUISE; 'shipwrecked' rearranges CRUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to utter profanities.

clue.text: Big shot heard in the ministry

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken, giving one spelled differently

parts.note: a cannon fires a big shot

explanation.surface: A celebrity spotted working in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big shot' suggests an important person, but it is artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral clergyman holds office in the church.

clue.text: Bean for a red-faced athlete

explanation.surface: A sprinter blushing like a bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing bean with scarlet flowers, and literally a sprinter who is flushed.

clue.text: Burning round the track?

explanation.surface: A driver speeding around the racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Very hot; and going very fast, as a car at speed.
